{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study describes a pipeline for quantitative analysis of heart histopathology in both mice and humans, comparing results between a disease model (TAC) and control, and between human patients with and without aortic stenosis. It quantifies morphological changes (cardiomyocyte size, nuclei size, capillary density, protein expression) and presents these as quantitative measures, thus fitting the criteria for inclusion.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study compares histopathology analyses of the heart in animal models and patients, focusing on cellular morphological changes like hypertrophy, nuclear enlargement, capillary rarefaction, and fibrosis, to understand disease mechanisms.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on heart diseases, specifically analyzing cardiomyocyte size, capillary density, and related markers in the context of cardiac hypertrophy and aortic stenosis.",
  "model_type": "induced",
  "model_evidence": "The study uses Transverse-aortic constriction (TAC) in mice, which is an induced model of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly details experiments performed on C57BL/6N mice, including surgical induction of transverse-aortic constriction (TAC).",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study quantifies cardiomyocyte area, minimum Feret Diameter, cardiomyocyte nuclei area and MinFeret, capillary contacts per cardiomyocyte, and pro-ANP expression, which include both morphological measurements (secondary biomarkers) and potentially functional implications (primary hard endpoints if linked to outcomes)."
}
